summary: AgroFEN is an agroclimatic alert service that delivers personalized weather warnings straight to a farmer’s cell phone through a chat assistant. Every morning, it checks the forecast for the farmer’s location and sends only what matters for their specific crop, such as heat waves, frost or heavy rain, so decisions like irrigating, harvesting or protecting plants can be made on time. Smart automation keeps it running 24/7, and farmers only need to scan a QR code to start chatting, with no complicated apps or technical knowledge. It addresses a core challenge: small farmers lose harvests and income to extreme weather because climate information is too generic, too complex or too late to act on. By turning weather data into simple, timely, crop-specific advice, AgroFEN reduces losses, supports food security and helps communities adapt to climate change.
details:
What it does and how it works
AgroFEN is an agroclimatic alert assistant that works through chat on a farmer’s phone. The farmer scans a QR code and starts chatting, with no app to install. Every morning, the system checks the weather for the farmer’s location, matches it to their crop, and sends only what affects it: heat waves, frost, heavy rain and other events. It runs 24/7 through automation.

Benefits

  • Timely decisions on irrigation, planting, harvesting and crop protection.
  • Fewer financial losses from extreme weather.
  • Simple, non-technical messages with no data overload.
  • Easy access: one QR code and a chat the farmer already uses every day.

Expected impact
Less crop and income loss for small farmers, stronger food security, and better climate adaptation for rural communities. Because it is digital and automated, it can scale to many more users at low additional cost.

Tools and technologies
AgroFEN combines several open data sources with a spreadsheet and a chat assistant:

  • Weather data: Open-Meteo Weather Forecast API (forecasts) and Open-Meteo Flood API (river flood risk).
  • El Niño phenomenon: Coastal El Niño Index (ICEN) from the Geophysical Institute of Peru (IGP), to add regional climate context.
  • Database: Google Sheets, accessed through its API.
  • Assistant and automation: [state the chat or messaging platform, programming language, automation tool and hosting].
  • Promotional video: Python (Pillow and NumPy), FFmpeg and the Poppins typeface.

Creativity
AgroFEN brings climate information to the channel farmers already use, instead of asking them to learn a new platform. It combines forecasts, flood risk and El Niño status into one short, crop-specific alert, rather than showing general weather data. The QR code reduces access to a single step.

Factors the team considered

  • Accessibility: farmers with limited technical knowledge and connectivity, so everything happens in a chat with no app to install.
  • Relevance: only useful alerts for each crop, to avoid notification overload.
  • Timing: alerts every morning and constant availability so farmers can act in time.
  • Scalability: automation and open data sources that can serve many users at low cost.
  • Local context: use of the IGP’s ICEN, which reflects climate variability on Peru’s coast.

Two things I couldn’t complete from what you gave me:

  • Chat platform, language, automation and hosting: these are in brackets. Tell me which ones you use and I’ll fill them in.
  • NASA data: none of the sources you shared come from NASA. If AgroFEN uses NASA POWER or another NASA resource, add it here and also in the “NASA Data” section of the form, since it’s required for the Global Award.
